policy: Critical and High issues in Open, In Progress or Pending Review block development freeze and every later phase. Numerical passes cannot close an issue. Fixed or Accepted requires committed closure evidence.

reproduction.description: Use the exact P3a production deformation path with all r95 shoulder correctives active; inspect the full elevation arc.

issues.defect: Long membrane-like axillary wall and deep chest-to-arm trench.
issues.acceptance: Anterior and posterior folds remain distinct, concave and volume-continuous without a planar membrane or knife-edge trench at every elevation sample.

reproduction.description: Raise both arms through the production press arc and compare the chest-rooted anterior fold against the humeral motion.

issues.defect: Excessive lateral pectoral tissue is transported with the humerus instead of preserving a chest-rooted anterior fold.
issues.acceptance: Pectoral mass remains chest-rooted while its humeral insertion and anterior fold lengthen smoothly through flexion and abduction.

reproduction.description: Compare neutral and overhead chest silhouettes using identical camera and render settings.

issues.defect: Lateral chest collapses while central pectoral volume balloons during overhead elevation.
issues.acceptance: Chest volume redistributes gradually without lateral collapse, central ballooning or an abrupt pectoral boundary.

reproduction.description: Inspect rear and inferior oblique views through elevation with the scapular corrective both isolated and combined.

issues.defect: Posterior fold lacks latissimus/teres support and reads as a pointed flap or cloth-like drape.
issues.acceptance: Posterior fold retains supported latissimus/teres volume with no detached flap, ledge or cape-like sheet.

reproduction.description: Inspect the neutral close-up silhouette and light roll around the shoulder cap.

issues.defect: Deltoid is an oversized spherical cap with inadequate anterior, middle and posterior regional definition.
issues.acceptance: Deltoid volume blends into clavicle, scapular spine and humerus with a plausible non-spherical resting contour.

reproduction.description: Follow the shoulder-to-arm silhouette from rest through elevation and rotation.

issues.defect: Abrupt narrowing, pinch and surface discontinuity at the deltoid/upper-arm transition.
issues.acceptance: The transition preserves a continuous load-bearing silhouette without pinching or a sudden cross-section change.

reproduction.description: Sample flexion and abduction arcs and compare surface motion with the measured multi-joint shoulder-complex pattern.

issues.defect: Clavicle, scapula and trapezius surface lack convincing coupled motion and supported volume.
issues.acceptance: Surface landmarks respond continuously to clavicular, scapular and glenohumeral motion without a fixed-ratio or rigid-sheet appearance.

reproduction.description: Use a symmetric pose and compare mirrored landmarks, silhouettes and corrective activation.

issues.defect: Left and right shoulder/axilla deformation is inconsistent in a symmetric overhead pose.
issues.acceptance: Mirrored inputs produce equivalent activation and surface deformation within declared tolerance, absent intentional asymmetry.

issues.region: fingers and thumb during equipment grip

reproduction.description: Inspect phalanx sequencing, thumb opposition, palm arch and contact around each equipment diameter.

issues.defect: Uniform finger curl, weak thumb opposition and implausible handle conformance.
issues.acceptance: Finger flexion must vary by joint and object diameter rather than using a uniform copied curl; thumb opposition is reviewed separately and equipment contact remains stable across curl-handle and pull-up-bar diameters.

reproduction.description: Trace equipment or floor load from hand through wrist into forearm under flexed and extended wrist conditions.

issues.defect: Wrist and handle alignment is unstable and does not form a convincing load path into the forearm.
issues.acceptance: Wrist alignment, forearm rotation and hand contact form a continuous load path; extended-wrist push-up loading may not be represented by an arbitrary hand rotation or collapsing wrist surface, and grip poses must preserve coherent wrist-to-forearm alignment.

reproduction.description: Compare the historical Phase 4 record and numeric status with the exact production-path images rejected by the owner.

issues.defect: The workflow allowed numerical/freeze completion despite unresolved obvious anatomy in committed review images.
issues.acceptance: Every Critical/High visual issue is fail-closed, evidence-bound and blocks freeze or later phases until committed closure evidence passes visual, numerical and regression review.

reproduction.description: For each anatomical coupling system in ORIGINAL_V1_ANATOMICAL_COUPLING_MAP.json, inspect exact candidate-bound weights-only and corrected motion across outbound/intermediate/endpoint/return samples.

issues.defect: The project has not yet candidate-proven whole-body shared-tissue coupling: a body part can still numerically pass while skin/muscle spanning multiple anatomical attachments is incorrectly owned or dragged by one joint/bone.
issues.acceptance: Every required coupling system is candidate-bound and proves all relevant attachment sides, weights-only deformation, intermediate/return motion, visual continuity, numerical regression and contact/load propagation where applicable; no Critical/High coupling defect remains open.
